properties.description: An ordered list of elements, arranged according to a certain rule or pattern.

properties.description: A sequence of numbers in which the difference between consecutive terms is constant.
A sequence of numbers where each term after the first is found by multiplying the previous term by a fixed, non-zero number called the 'common ratio,' denoted by r.
properties.example: In the sequence 3, 6, 12, 24, … the common ratio r is 2.

properties.description: A series of numbers in which each is the sum of the two preceding ones, usually starting with 0 and 1.

properties.application: This ratio appears in various aspects of art, architecture, and nature.

properties.description: collections of distinct elements
A collection of distinct objects.
An element either belongs or does not belong.
A set with no elements.
The number of elements in a set.
A set A is equivalent to a set B if the following conditions hold: every element of A is an element of B, and every element of B is an element of A.
A set A is considered a subset of set B if every element of set A is also an element of set B.
If A is a subset of B, and A is not equal to B (meaning some element in B is not in A), then A is called a proper subset of B.
properties.example: •If A={a,b} and B={a,b,c,d,e}, then A⊂B because A is a subset of B, and there exist the elements in B (which are c, d, e) that are not in A.
